newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Emerging market funds favour Mexico, SKorea, India.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market funds favour Mexico, SKorea, India.

text.p: A survey of mutual fund asset allocations showed Mexico was the favourite destination for global emerging market equity funds this year, followed by South Korea, India, South Africa and Brazil.

The survey result was announced at an international investment conference in Geneva by Christopher Poll, chairman of Micropal, a London-based market analysis company which tracks 38,000 mutual funds in the $6.5 trillion global fund industry.
Poll said the research is based on data provided by mutual funds although he said some banks declined to supply information on how their fund managers allocated assets.
He said money flowed into Asia rather than Latin America in the past 12 months, although Russia and East Europe also enjoyed big increases in fund flows.

In regional terms, Asia enjoyed the biggest inflow of global fund money in the past 12 months with $2.56 billion, followed by Latin America with $1.53 billion and East Europe and Africa with $1.08 billion, the survey showed.
In the emerging markets league, Micropal research showed global equity market fund managers poured a net $758 million into Mexico in the past 12 months, Poll said.
Mexico was followed by $752 million with South Korea, $708 million with India, $584 million with South Africa and $570 million with Brazil.
In the same period, Argentina and Malaysia markets suffered net outflows of $68 million and $34 million respectively.
Another trend which emerged was that regional money managers in Asia put more faith into China and Hong Kong than their global counterparts.
Global fund managers placed only $152 million in China and Hong Kong in the past 12 months compared to $914 million invested by Asian regional funds, Poll said.
In Latin America, regional emerging market fund flows into Brazil, Peru, Argentina, Chile and Colombia were negative.

The research also showed that the assets of open-ended U.S. emerging market funds ballooned to $18.9 billion in February 1996 from a mere $30 million in December 1990. Adjusted, this represented more than $15 billion of new money over 38 months.
Looking back to the behaviour of U.S. investors, Poll said their net selling between January 1991 and September 1996 averaged only 1.11 percent of total assets a month.

The American investor did not panic during the Mexico crisis in late 1994, withdrawing a net $500 million from funds but reinvesting more than $700 million shortly afterwards to use the fallback as a buying opportunity, Poll added.
